messages:
maria-hwang: quick heads up — after the latest kernel-selection change we started seeing a spike in workspace OOMs on p3-like instances. repro on staging when sequence len > 1024 and batch jitter is high. attaching quick perf notes below.

aj-patel: can you paste the profiler snapshot? is this prefill or mostly decode-time faults?

maria-hwang: profiler shows most faults during decode path after prefill completes — kv cache pressure + fragmented slab allocations. flame graph: decode -> attention_kernV2 -> workspace_alloc. also saw >2x malloc stalls in the allocator.

srinath-kr: hmm, sounds like kernel V2 uses slightly bigger temporary buffers per-token. combined with continuous batching jitter we're losing packing efficiency. could be the kernel selection heuristic chose V2 for latency but cost us workspace headroom.

katie-lee: timeline: kernel switch rolled 03:12, repro started ~03:18, spikes peaked at 03:24. we also had a small increase in 1k-2k token requests from a churny client.

ryan-m: short-term mitigation: we can force fallback to the previous kernel on the affected model geometry until we tune allocator heuristics. also consider a per-request workspace soft-cap so a single request can't bloat slab fragmentation.

maria-hwang: filed a canary rule: put kernel=legacy for model X in region us-west-2. want to avoid broad rollback if possible.

aj-patel: for allocator tuning ideas: 1) add a tiny-sized freelist class to reduce fragmentation for 8-64KB scratch buffers, 2) enable opportunistic coalesce of adjacent free blocks every N frees, 3) add a reclaim hook triggered when decode path spikes vs baseline.

srinath-kr: agree. also we should test "workspace pinning" where we pin a small pool of buffers to high-throughput decoders to avoid churn. pin pool size should be proportional to expected in-flight tokens (estimate = avg_batch * avg_seq * per-token-scratch).

katie-lee: curious about KV cache side — is eviction policy interacting? we saw a lot of demotions right before OOMs. maybe prefill caches are holding onto larger segments, then decode path tries to prefill more and fails.

maria-hwang: yep — sequence: prefill reserves KV segments -> contiguous slab fragmentation -> decode needs temp buffers -> allocator stalls -> OOM. Observed cache demotions at high-water mark then immediate prefill attempts.

ryan-m: sounds like prefill vs decode contention. two experiments: A) introduce per-request KV soft-cap (e.g., --kv-soft-cap=24MB) to let decode reclaim some headroom, B) add hysteresis to prefill so it won't allocate if free workspace < threshold.

aj-patel: we should also consider splitting KV cache into small fixed-size arena buckets for the hot prefixes, and a large, coalescing arena for cold entries. that reduces fragmentation from variable sized prefill segments.

srinath-kr: quick profiling task list: 1) run microbench with controlled jittered batches, 2) compare kernel V1 vs V2 workspace allocation sizes, 3) enable coalesce and measure free-list churn, 4) measure tail-latency regressions with soft-cap. I'll queue the jobs.

perf-bot: perf summary (automated): job 1768999000: kernel-V2 increases per-request scratch by ~18% median; allocator stall time +120%; OOM rate x3 on jittered load.

maria-hwang: thanks perf-bot — can we also get a heap-dump of the slab layout at OOM time? need to see fragmentation pattern.

katie-lee: I'll add a debug flag that dumps slab histogram and KV segment map when free < 5% and OOM imminent. will post link.

ryan-m: for immediate prod safety: deploy per-request KV soft-cap to 32MB and enable prefill hysteresis for the affected model. fallback kernel stays enabled in canary for now. monitor tail-latency.

aj-patel: note: soft-cap must be soft — deny only when downstream SLO would be impacted. prefer degrade prefill fidelity (fewer segments) vs hard rejection. add metrics: kv_evictions_due_to_softcap and prefill_reductions.

srinath-kr: follow-up items assigned: allocator freelist patch (aj), slab-coalesce toggle (srinath), prefill hysteresis + soft-cap (katie), canary kernel rollback rule (maria), perf runs and heap-dumps (ryan).

maria-hwang: thanks all. I'll coordinate rollout timeline. tagging @ops for watch. :eyes: 

katie-lee: quick note — if we add pinned pools, watch out for long-lived pinned buffers increasing steady-state memory. need an eviction policy for pins too.

ryan-m: agreed. propose an LRU pin fallback after inactivity window.

maria-hwang: closing thread for now — will update when we have profiler + heap-dump links. :thumbsup:
